title: Coherence of an epimorphic quotient with quasi-compact kernel pair
statement: Let $\mathcal E$ be a coherent Grothendieck topos [def-trf-coherent-topos] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $p:P\to A$ be an epimorphism in $\mathcal E$, with $P$ coherent. If its kernel-pair object $R=P\times_A P$ is quasi-compact, then $A$ is coherent. Here the two projections $R\rightrightarrows P$ are the pullback of $p$ with itself; epimorphism means right cancellation against every object of $\mathcal E$, and quasi-compact and coherent have exactly the meanings in [def-trf-coherent-topos].

source.place: Agent-formulated auxiliary for the finite-presentation argument, using Tag 0GMP (lemma-image-of-quasi-compact), Tag 00WN (lemma-mono-epi-sheaves) and Tag 00W2 (lemma-limit-sheaf). These tags supply the sheaf ingredients, not a verbatim statement of the coherent quotient criterion. Context: literature/illusie-laszlo-orgogozo-travaux-de-gabber_arXiv-1207.3648.pdf, Exposé XI, proof of Lemma 2.5, printed p. 179; complete proposed argument in report.md.

proof.text: Work in a small-site presentation of $\mathcal E$ supplied by [def-trf-coherent-topos]. Epimorphisms are stable under pullback: a local lift of a section, provided by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-locally-surjective], combines with its given section in the other factor by sectionwise pullbacks [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise]. The coproduct of any family of sheaves is the sheafification of their presheaf coproduct: the sheafification adjunction [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] identifies maps out of it with families of maps from the summands. Every section of this coproduct locally comes from a summand by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local]. Consequently a jointly epimorphic family is exactly a family in which every target section locally lifts into one member; this condition is stable under pullback. Indeed local surjectivity of its coproduct map gives a local coproduct section, and a further covering gives a section of one summand; the converse is immediate from the same criterion.

proof.text: An epimorphic image of a quasi-compact object is quasi-compact. For an epimorphism $e:X\to Y$ with $X$ quasi-compact, pull a jointly epimorphic family over $Y$ back to $X$ by step 1 and select finitely many members. If two maps from $Y$ agree on these selected members, they agree after $e$ by their pulled-back epimorphy, and hence agree by cancellation with $e$. Thus the selected family is epic over $Y$. Also a finite coproduct of quasi-compact objects is quasi-compact: pull any jointly epic family back to each summand, select finitely many indices for each, and take the finite union; right cancellation on every summand proves joint epimorphy. The empty coproduct is quasi-compact as well: any two maps from the initial object agree, so the empty subfamily already is epic.

proof.text: Fix the small full generating family $\mathcal G$ of coherent objects closed under finite limits from [def-trf-coherent-topos]. Every quasi-compact object $X$ has a finite jointly epimorphic family $G_i\to X$ with $G_i\in\mathcal G$: start with the generating epimorphism from a coproduct and use the definition of quasi-compactness to select finitely many summands. More generally, for any epimorphism $E\to X$ with $X$ quasi-compact, first take a generating family $G_t\to E$. The composite family to $X$ is jointly epic (composition of epimorphisms), so finitely many of its members cover $X$; each selected map still has its specified lift to $E$. The finite family can be empty. All index sets lie in the containing universe of [def-weil-size-convention].

proof.text: Since the coherent object $P$ is quasi-compact and $p:P\to A$ is epic, step 2 shows that $A$ is quasi-compact. It remains to check the quasi-separatedness condition for arbitrary quasi-compact $B,C$ with maps to $A$. Choose finite jointly epimorphic families $G_i\to B$ and $H_j\to C$ from $\mathcal G$ by step 3. By step 1 the finite family $G_i\times_A H_j\to B\times_A C$ is jointly epic: first pull the $G_i$ family back along $B\times_A C\to B$, then pull back the $H_j$ family along the resulting maps to $C$. Hence, by step 2, it suffices to prove that every $G_i\times_A H_j$ is quasi-compact.

source.place: Tags 00WN (lemma-mono-epi-sheaves), 00W2 (lemma-limit-sheaf), 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification), 0GMP (lemma-image-of-quasi-compact), 0GMQ (lemma-coproduct-quasi-compact): agent expansion of the coherent quotient criterion in the finite-presentation argument.

proof.text: Fix one pair $G=G_i$, $H=H_j$. The pullback $P\times_A G\to G$ is epic by step 1. Apply the lifted finite-generator presentation of step 3 to this epimorphism: obtain finitely many $K_a\in\mathcal G$ with a jointly epimorphic family $K_a\to G$, together with maps $k_a:K_a\to P$ satisfying $p k_a=(G\to A)(K_a\to G)$. Likewise obtain $L_b\to H$ jointly epic with lifts $l_b:L_b\to P$. By successive pullbacks of these two jointly epic families, the finite family $K_a\times_A L_b\to G\times_A H$ is jointly epic.

source.place: Tags 00WN (lemma-mono-epi-sheaves), 00W2 (lemma-limit-sheaf), 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification), 0GMP (lemma-image-of-quasi-compact), 0GMQ (lemma-coproduct-quasi-compact): agent expansion of the coherent quotient criterion in the finite-presentation argument.

proof.text: For each $a,b$, view $R$ over $P$ by its first projection $r_1$ and also by its second projection $r_2$. The universal property of the kernel pair identifies $$K_a\times_A L_b\simeq (K_a\times_{k_a,P,r_1}R)\times_{r_2,P,l_b}L_b.$$ Indeed, by sectionwise limits [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-limits-sectionwise] a section of the right side over an object of the site is a quadruple $(x,(u,v),y)$ with $x$ a section of $K_a$, $(u,v)$ a section of $R$ (so $pu=pv$), $y$ a section of $L_b$, $u=k_a(x)$ and $v=l_b(y)$. It is determined by $(x,y)$, which is subject exactly to $pk_a(x)=pl_b(y)$; this is the condition defining a section of the left side, compatibly with restrictions, so the identification is natural. Now $K_a$ is quasi-compact, being a coherent object of $\mathcal G$, and $R$ is quasi-compact by hypothesis. Since $P$ is coherent, it is quasi-separated, so the definition of quasi-separatedness in [def-trf-coherent-topos] makes $K_a\times_P R$ quasi-compact. Apply the same definition again to the quasi-compact objects $K_a\times_P R$, over $P$ by $r_2$, and $L_b$, over $P$ by $l_b$. Hence $K_a\times_A L_b$ is quasi-compact; quasi-compactness passes along the isomorphism, since an isomorphism is an epimorphism (step 2). Only the quasi-separatedness of $P$ itself is used here; no coherence of a product of coherent objects is needed.

source.place: Tags 00WN (lemma-mono-epi-sheaves), 00W2 (lemma-limit-sheaf), 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification), 0GMP (lemma-image-of-quasi-compact), 0GMQ (lemma-coproduct-quasi-compact): agent expansion of the coherent quotient criterion in the finite-presentation argument.

proof.text: Step 2 applied to the finite jointly epic family of step 5 now makes $G\times_A H$ quasi-compact. Applied to the finite jointly epic family of step 4, it makes $B\times_A C$ quasi-compact. This holds for every quasi-compact $B,C$ over $A$, exactly the quasi-separatedness definition in [def-trf-coherent-topos]. The quasi-compactness of $A$ from step 4 therefore proves that $A$ is coherent. Empty finite families cause no exception because the empty coproduct case was included in step 2.
